Loss-of-function mutations in ALS2 disrupt its role in Rab5-mediated endosomal trafficking, which in turn impairs the autophagy-lysosome pathway. This impairment leads to motor neuron dysfunction and degeneration, manifesting as spastic paralysis in infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis and motor neuron degeneration characteristic of juvenile amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 2.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ALS2 with a clear gain-of-function or dominant-negative mechanism would falsify this hypothesis.
